notes: SHIP v1.14.400 - M1-d: THE READ SIDE. M1 COMPLETE. Until this ship there was no safeGet and no safeRemove, so all 121 getItem and all 31 removeItem calls were raw BY CONSTRUCTION, and every parse failure in the app degraded silently to null, {} or []. There was no corrupt-data toast, no quarantine, and no your-data-looked-damaged path anywhere in PHANTOM. That contradicted the app's own first rule for the ONE case that destroys user data rather than merely hiding a surface: a damaged blob read through safeParse returned an empty array, and the very next save wrote that empty array back over it. Silent, total, permanent - and the technician's only clue would have been work that quietly stopped existing. THE DISTINCTION THAT MAKES THIS WORK. ABSENT is normal and stays silent. PRESENT BUT UNPARSEABLE is a data-loss event: it is now loud, and the bytes are kept. safeGet(key, fallback) reads, parses, and on failure hands the raw string to phantom_quarantine() before returning the fallback. Quarantine records the key, timestamp, byte length, truncation flag and parser error alongside up to 64KB of the original bytes, raises a throttled toast naming the key, and logs it. It reads its own store with a RAW parse rather than through safeGet, so a corrupt quarantine cannot recurse into quarantining itself, and it is wrapped so it can never throw back into a read path. The quarantine key is registered in the backup: damaged data is still the technician's data and is now the only surviving copy of it. safeRemove(key) returns false and says so rather than throwing into a caller that assumed deletion succeeded. THE MIGRATION WAS MECHANICAL AND VERIFIED, NOT HAND-EDITED. 84 call sites matched two exact shapes - safeParse(localStorage.getItem(X) || 'literal', FB) and safeParse(localStorage.getItem(X), FB) - where X is a bare identifier or a quoted literal. A script performed the swap, reported the count per shape, confirmed ZERO complex shapes remained, and checked that the open-paren and close-paren deltas matched (-84 / -84) before writing anything, aborting otherwise. 84 swapped, 0 leftover. Spot-verified at the sites that matter most: the node-status wrapper, all four deploy loaders (deployments, racks, phases, optics, audit) and ge_load. An earlier attempt to run this transform inline through the shell mangled its own regex through heredoc escaping and was rewritten as a real script file - the file was never touched by the broken version. WHAT IS DELIBERATELY STILL RAW: 41 getItem calls remain, and they are correct as-is. Two are inside the hardened layer itself and MUST be raw (safeGet's own read, and quarantine's self-read). The rest read RAW STRINGS rather than JSON - phantom_legacy compared against '1', the session and freeze blobs, the LZString-compressed Master - where a JSON-parsing door is the wrong door. Routing those would be a change of meaning, not a hardening. GATES: 3 inline blocks compile clean x3, CSS braces 4557/4557, line endings preserved, 29 registry keys with no duplicates, three-stamp lockstep. M1 IS NOW COMPLETE: backup coverage derived from a registry (.397), coverage measured against live storage rather than asserted (.398), every write path guarded and offline PDF import working (.399), and the read path hardened with an honest corrupt-data route (.400). Deferred with reasons on record: the six dead else-localStorage.setItem arms (unreachable, safeStore is declared above all of them) and the handoffDraft truthiness bug at the phantom_handoff_v1 read, which is a logic defect rather than a storage one and belongs with the Shift work in M4. DEVICE-VERIFY: (1) normal use - nothing should look different anywhere. (2) In Safari console run localStorage.setItem('phantom_audits_v1','{{{broken') then reload: expect a toast naming phantom_audits_v1, the app still working, and localStorage.getItem('phantom_quarantine_v1') containing the original broken bytes. (3) Export a backup and confirm phantom_quarantine_v1 travels in it.
